mappings.note: Which remedy the poet offers for building confidence -- taking the easy task first, his counsel rather than a quoted line. Rejected LO-73: nothing states it as a fact.
What we should do on the strength of these kundaliyas -- the poems' usefulness. Rejected LO-70: the item asks what they are for, not what the poet holds.
What the poet means to say THROUGH the line 'chitt mein khata na paavai' -- his claim about a clear conscience. Rejected LO-76, which I keep for glossing the phrase itself.
The result of unconsidered work -- spoilt work, the world's laughter, a lasting sting, all in the verse. Rejected LO-72: consequences, not the poem's use.
Explicate the sense of the whole 'bina bichaare jo karai' kundaliya -- the poet's stated idea. Rejected LO-74: the demand is the meaning, not the verse form.
What that kundaliya teaches us -- its usefulness. Rejected LO-70, used for the item asking its sense.
Which counsel the line 'beeti taahi bisaari de' gives -- the poet's advice. Rejected LO-76: a whole line's argument, not a word.
Which troubles follow thoughtless action -- a list the learner collects from the verses. Rejected LO-72: the troubles, not the poems' purpose.
HOW the poet conveys the loss of peace -- reading his method of stating it through food, honour and revelry. Rejected LO-73: the item asks about his handling, not for a fact.
Why the poems still speak to us -- their continuing usefulness. Rejected LO-74: the item asks about relevance, not about the folk form.
The marks of his language -- plain, folk-near, and memorable 'like proverbs', which is appreciation of the oral-traditional idiom. Rejected LO-76: a whole style, not a word.
The view of life the two kundaliyas together put forward -- the poet's outlook. Rejected LO-72: his position, not the text's use.
The chief message of both poems -- their usefulness stated whole. Rejected LO-70, used where the item asks his outlook rather than the message.
Why deliberate action is needed -- the poet's reasoning. Rejected LO-73: argued, not located.
What the poet TEACHES about the consequences -- the key ends at learning from one's mistakes, which is the poem's use. Rejected LO-73: the consequences themselves are asked elsewhere.
Which life-value the poem gives us -- its usefulness. Rejected LO-70: the item asks what we take from it.

How the message of 'samujhi beeti so beeti' can be applied in OUR lives -- taking up the poet's idea against one's own experience. Rejected LO-72: the demand is a personal application, not a statement of use.
What importance this maxim has in YOUR life -- explicitly measuring the poet's idea against the learner's own experience. Rejected LO-71: no preference is being argued for.

Distinguishes 'chitt mein chain na paavai' from 'chitt mein khata na paavai' -- two near-identical phrases told apart, exactly the fine grain of language. Rejected LO-70: the difference is lexical before it is conceptual.
The worth of a considered and unforced life, per the poet -- his proposition. Rejected LO-72: his view, not the text's use.
Which ill effects the poem names -- regret, spoilt work, mockery, joylessness, all in the verses. Rejected LO-72: the effects, not the purpose.
What the poet would advise someone who cannot let the past go -- applying his idea to a case. Rejected LO-73: no line answers for this situation.
Which life-values the poem yields -- prudence, patience, positivity: its usefulness. Rejected LO-70: what we gain, not what he holds.
What follows unconsidered work, from the printed extract. Rejected LO-70: stated in the lines.
When a person's work is spoilt -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-70: stated.
What happens once work is spoilt (the world laughs). Rejected LO-70: stated.
When a person must repent -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-70: stated.
The result of thoughtless work (it is spoilt). Rejected LO-72: a consequence, not the poem's use.
What the poet means by 'beeti taahi bisaari de aage ki sudhi lei' -- his counsel. Rejected LO-76: a whole line's argument.
What to do having forgotten the past -- think of the future, the poet's prescription. Rejected LO-73: general counsel.
Which works to set the mind on (those that come easily) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-70, kept for the items that argue why.
The message this kundaliya gives -- its usefulness. Rejected LO-70: what it is for, not what he thinks.
What must be done to be happy hereafter -- the poet's counsel to resolve and move on. Rejected LO-73: a prescription, not a located fact.
What the thoughtless man does not get (peace) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-70: stated.
Sense of the phrase 'jag mein hot hansaay' -- glossing an archaic construction. Rejected LO-73: lexical.
The poem's main message (act with thought) -- its usefulness. Rejected LO-70: the message, not his handling of it.
HOW the poet censures thoughtlessness -- reading the way he builds the reproach. Rejected LO-73: his method, not a fact.
Meaning of 'raag rang manahin na bhaavai' -- glossing an archaic phrase. Rejected LO-70, kept for whole-line propositions.
Whom the poet addresses with 'yahai karu man parteeti' -- located by close reading of the couplet. Rejected LO-76: the phrase is quoted, not glossed.
From what happiness comes, per the poet -- attending to what lies ahead, his claim. Rejected LO-73: argued.
When the ill-natured do not mock -- when the work goes naturally, stated in the extract. Rejected LO-70: located.
